description:
In one of the greatest hockey rivalries of all-time, Peter Forsberg and the Colorado Avalanche got the best of Detroit in 1996 during the Western Conference Final on their way to their first ever Stanley Cup victory. Leading the series 3-2 on home ice in Game 6, Forsberg scores a beautiful goal that puts the game out of reach for the Red Wings. Late in the second period with a two-goal lead, Forsberg pounces on a Detroit turnover on the left boards. He stickhandles through Nicklas Lidstrom before shooting it past the netminder for his seventh goal of the playoffs.

description:
In the 1994 Stanley Cup Final against the Vancouver Canucks, Mark Messier delivered the decisive goal that secured the Stanley Cup. Holding a 2-1 lead in the middle of the second period during Game 7, the New York Rangers were on a power play. Sergei Zubov faked a shot, instead passing it down to Brian Noonan. Noonan then lofted the puck towards the net, sparking a frenzied scramble for possession. Amid the chaos, Messier skillfully located the puck and managed to tap it past the opposing goaltender. The goal proved to be the game-winner in a thrilling 3-2 victory, giving the Rangers their first Stanley Cup since 1940, ending a 54-year drought.

description:
Amid the Montreal Canadiens' record-setting journey to the 1993 Stanley Cup Final, Patrick Roy showcased brilliance as he anchored his team to championship glory. In a pivotal moment during Game 4 of the Final in Los Angeles, with the score deadlocked, Roy made a crucial save on Luc Robitaille with just over one minute left in the third period. As Roy secured the rebound with his glove, Tomas Sandstrom attempted to pry it loose with a poke but was unsuccessful. The perpetually confident goaltender responded with a wink and a smile, leaving an indelible mark on the situation. The Canadiens later won Game 4 in overtime, securing a commanding 3-1 series lead, which they sealed with a home victory in the next game. Roy's outstanding contributions throughout the 1993 playoffs – during which he won a record 10 overtime games and posted a .929 save percentage along with a 2.13 goals-against average – earned him the Conn Smythe Trophy. It was his second of three playoff MVPs during his career.

description:

description:
After losing Game 1 of the 1999 Western Conference Final at home, Dallas couldn’t afford another defeat before the series shifted to Colorado. Up 3-2 late in the third period on a power play, Mike Modano makes sure Dallas is heading out with a victory. As Dallas players move the puck around, Modano pops out from the slot to the right side of the umbrella formation. Now near the top of the circle, he receives the pass from Sergei Zubov. There, he plays a beautiful give-and-go with Zubov and roofs it up top over Patrick Roy. The goal proved to be the final one of the game in a 4-2 Stars win. Dallas went on to win the series in seven games and then beat Buffalo in six for their first Stanley Cup. Modano led all Stars players in playoff points that year with 23 which was second in the League.

description:
During the 1995 Stanley Cup Final, the smooth-skating Scott Niedermayer scores a huge tying goal in Game 2 versus the Detroit Red Wings. Down 2-1 with just over ten minutes remaining in the third period, Niedermayer goes end-to-end skating swiftly through the Detroit players before he pulls up near the top of the circles to send a wrister that goes wide. Bouncing off the boards, the puck kicks back out to the front where Niedermayer follows up to bank it home. The goal on the road tied the game and propelled New Jersey to a victory for a 2-0 series lead. The Devils would later clinch the series at home with a 4-0 sweep for their first ever Stanley Cup.

description:
After scoring the overtime winner in Game 6 of the 1993 Clarence Campbell Conference Final versus Toronto to force Game 7, Wayne Gretzky nets a hat trick to advance the Kings to their first ever Stanley Cup Final appearance. The scoring begins with a 2-on-1 with Marty McSorley where it’s a give-and-go play before Gretzky taps it in for the shorthanded tally. Then on his second goal, Gretzky gets the drop pass from Tomas Sandstrom before skating to the middle of the ice and sending a clapper past Felix Potvin. Gretzky’s final goal was a play where he was behind the goal line and threw the puck out in front of the net. The puck redirected off of a Toronto skate and into the net for a two-goal lead with just over three minutes remaining in the game. Although the Kings would lose in the Stanley Cup Final that season to the Montreal Canadiens, Gretzky had an incredible playoff run registering 40 points which led all players.

description:
With four minutes remaining in the third period of a tie game, captain Steve Yzerman goes end-to-end to score a massive unassisted goal for the game-winner in Game 2 in Denver vs. rival and reigning Stanley Cup champion Colorado. The captain picks up the puck below the goal line and evades a forechecker before speeding up the ice. Entering the offensive zone with speed, he goes down the left wall on his backhand and then quickly shifts it to his forehand to get the shot off. The rebound kicks out behind the net where Yzerman banks it off Patrick Roy’s pad. Earning the split in the series on the road helped Detroit gain momentum and confidence in finally beating their nemesis, earning a trip to the Stanley Cup Final where they swept Philadelphia to end the franchise’s 42-year Cup drought.

description:

That year marked Kurri’s last Stanley Cup win which was his fifth (all with Edmonton) in a span of only seven years.

description:
During Game 4 of the 1997 Stanley Cup Final, with a 1-0 lead in the second period, Darren McCarty crafts an astonishing game-winning moment, securing the Detroit Red Wings' first Stanley Cup victory since 1955, thus ending a 42-year drought. McCarty's remarkable goal, his third in the playoffs, unfolded with finesse. Commencing in the defensive zone, the Red Wings assert their dominance along the boards to gain possession. Tomas Sandstrom feeds McCarty in the neutral zone, setting up a 1-on-1 opportunity. McCarty astounds by executing an inside-to-outside maneuver, breezing past the defenseman. Finally, with a deft touch, he places the puck beyond the outstretched reach of Ron Hextall, eliciting a roaring eruption from the crowd. This unforgettable play symbolizes not only a triumph on the ice but also the culmination of years of anticipation for the Red Wings and their devoted fans.
